clue.text: He suffered irreparable damage when shell landed

definitions.text: He suffered irreparable damage when shell landed

parts.words: He suffered irreparable damage when shell landed
parts.note: reads like a soldier hit by an artillery shell, but the shell is an eggshell: the nursery-rhyme egg who fell off a wall and could not be put together again

explanation.walkthrough: 'Shell' suggests war and bombardment; the victim is the egg character of the nursery rhyme, whom all the king's horses and men could not mend.
explanation.definitionFit: The nursery-rhyme egg fell from a wall and broke beyond repair, so his shell landing ruined him for good.

clue.text: It's easy to hold, hard control

definitions.meaning: a small amount that fits in one hand
said of an unruly person who is difficult to manage

explanation.walkthrough: The page shows a gap between 'hard' and 'control', where a short word such as 'to' seems to have been lost in printing; the second sense is 'hard to control'.
explanation.definitionFit: A small quantity fits in the palm and is easy to hold; a difficult child or person is also called this, being hard to control.

clue.text: Spots me with tame lioness, climbing to the top of Snowdon

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down entry, climbing means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: Elsa was the tame lioness of the book and film Born Free

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter

explanation.surface: A child's spotty rash blamed on a pet lioness scrambling up Snowdon, the highest mountain in Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns ELSA into ASLE; 'to the top of' takes the first letter of Snowdon. 'with' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The illness is known for its red rash, so the disease is named by its symptom of spots.

clue.text: Make an inventory, as rustlers do

definitions.meaning: to count and list the goods held
rustlers steal cattle, the farmer's livestock

explanation.definitionFit: Counting goods in stock is a shopkeeper's audit; cattle thieves literally steal livestock.

clue.text: They are due to, firstly, those coming out and about

indicators.note: about means going around something, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: debs, short for debutantes, are young women coming out into society

indicators.note: firstly asks for just the opening letter of the word to

explanation.surface: Something owed to a group of people emerging from somewhere, with a muddle of directions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firstly' takes T from 'to', and 'about' puts DEBS around it. Debutantes 'come out' when they are first presented in society.
explanation.definitionFit: Money owed is money due to be paid back to creditors.

clue.text: Wonder if transport is held up during race, perhaps

indicators.note: during means inside the span of, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a mile is a classic race distance, an example of a race

indicators.note: in a down entry, held up means the word is raised, so read from bottom to top

parts.note: a car is a means of transport

explanation.surface: Wondering whether traffic will be delayed while a race is on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held up' reverses the vehicle, as a down entry reads upwards, and 'during' sets it inside the race distance. 'Wonder' looks like a verb but is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A miracle is a marvel, something that inspires astonishment.

clue.text: Traveller to ancient city, the first

parts.note: taken as written
Ur is the ancient Sumerian city in Mesopotamia
first is written 1st, with the digit read as the letter I

explanation.surface: Someone journeying to a long-ruined city, the earliest to go there.
explanation.definitionFit: A tourist is a sightseer on a trip, a kind of traveller.

clue.text: Alternatively, there's some point in one going in for sport

parts.note: alternatively is a stiff way of saying or
one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: in means one piece is put inside another

parts.note: going in is entering
a point of the compass, here east, E

explanation.surface: An argument that taking part in a game has some purpose after all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts E (a compass point) into ENTERING, making ENTEERING. 'point' tempts as 'purpose', but it is a compass bearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Orienteering is a competitive outdoor activity of navigating with map and compass between checkpoints.

clue.text: Search for smuggled liquor

parts.note: to run goods is to smuggle them, so smuggled is ran
sack is an old word for a dry white wine such as sherry

explanation.surface: Customs officers hunting for contraband alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link word. SACK is the sherry of Shakespeare's Falstaff; 'run' in the sense of smuggle gives RAN.
explanation.definitionFit: To ransack is to rummage thoroughly through a place, a rough search.

clue.text: Deposit gold in branch in town

indicators.note: deposit means put something down somewhere, here the gold is placed within the branch

parts.note: a bough is a large branch of a tree
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Banking gold at a local branch of a bank in town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'branch' suggests a bank's local office, fitting 'Deposit gold', but it is part of a tree; OR is the heraldic word for gold.
explanation.definitionFit: A borough is a town with its own corporation or local government.

clue.text: Hal, perhaps sighing for a Shavian role

parts.note: Hal is a familiar form of Henry, as Shakespeare's Prince Hal

indicators.note: perhaps here says the letters could be otherwise arranged

explanation.surface: Prince Hal sighing as he hankers after a part in a Bernard Shaw play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hal, perhaps' looks like a definition by example, but 'perhaps' belongs with 'sighing' as the anagram signal, giving HIGGINS. Shavian means of George Bernard Shaw.
explanation.definitionFit: The phonetics professor in Shaw's play Pygmalion is a character written by that playwright.

clue.text: Embraces and fondles promiscuously

indicators.note: promiscuously means indiscriminately and in disorder, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Hugging and caressing without much discrimination.
explanation.definitionFit: To enfold someone is to wrap them in one's arms, a hug.

clue.text: Bill's turned round — I jumped right, in part

indicators.note: jumped right says this letter hops further to the right in the word
turned round asks for the word to be read from end to start

parts.note: bills are posters, that is, notices
taken as written

explanation.surface: An account of a man's bill being reversed after he leapt to the right in some way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned round' reverses NOTICES to SECITON; then 'I jumped right' moves the I one place right to give the answer. 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A section is a portion or segment of a whole.

clue.text: Kipling's were plainly from the hills

definitions.text: Kipling's were plainly from the hills

parts.words: Kipling's were plainly from the hills
parts.note: alludes to Kipling's story collection Plain ... from the Hills, its title woven into the clue as 'plainly from the hills'

explanation.walkthrough: Kipling's first prose collection was Plain Tales from the Hills (1888), stories of British India; the clue hides the title in its wording.
explanation.definitionFit: The collection was a book of short stories, that is, narratives.

clue.text: In a rich way, only let up when broke

indicators.note: broke means smashed up, so these letters are broken and reassembled

explanation.surface: Living richly, only easing off once out of money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broke' reads as penniless, which fits the riches story, but signals the anagram. 'when' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Opulently means luxuriously or lavishly, the manner of the wealthy.

clue.text: Sworn at, round he turned

indicators.note: turned means spun round, so these letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone cursed at him, and he spun round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sworn at' looks like being cursed, but 'Sworn' alone is the definition and 'at, round he' is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Testimony given under oath is given as a sworn statement in court.

clue.text: Membership in need mostly set aside

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside another
mostly means not all of the word, so one letter is dropped

parts.note: need is taken as the word itself
split as member plus ship: an arm is a member of the body and an ark is a ship

explanation.surface: Club membership in hard times being mostly put on hold.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 'Membership' as member plus ship. 'mostly' here drops the first letter of 'need', leaving EED, which 'in' wraps round the member-and-ship pair.
explanation.definitionFit: Funds earmarked are reserved or allocated for a particular purpose.

clue.text: Let again, for free

definitions.meaning: to rent a property out a second time

explanation.definitionFit: To lease a property once more is to rent it out anew; to let a prisoner go is to liberate them.

clue.text: Rearing all over the place, and getting madder

indicators.note: all over the place means scattered in disorder, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A horse rearing wildly and growing more furious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and getting' are link words between the anagram and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Madder in the sense of more cross or furious, the comparative of being cross.

clue.text: Motorways to East and West of a city

indicators.note: to east and west of means placed either side, so the motorways surround the letter

parts.note: two M1s, the M1 being Britain's best-known motorway, with the 1 read as I

explanation.surface: Directions to a city with motorways leading off both ways.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds; one M1 on each side of A gives the Florida city.
explanation.definitionFit: The Florida resort is a major US city.

clue.text: In 1049, it raised first class citizen soldiers

parts.note: in Roman numerals M is 1000 and IL is used loosely for 49
taken as written

indicators.note: in a down entry, raised means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: first class is A1, with the digit read as the letter I

explanation.surface: Dating the founding of a citizen army to the year 1049.
explanation.walkthrough: 1049 as M + IL is a loose Roman numeral (strictly MXLIX). 'raised' turns AI into IA. 'In' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A militia is a body of civilians trained as part-time soldiers, called up in emergencies.

clue.text: Insect swallowing -fruit for nourishment

indicators.note: swallowing means taking something inside, so the insect encloses the fruit

parts.note: an ant is an insect
a lime is a citrus fruit

explanation.surface: A bug gulping down fruit to feed itself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Insect' looks like the subject of a little nature scene; the answer is an old word for food. 'for' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Aliment is an old word for food, what sustains the body.

clue.text: Criminal has bad time turning left

parts.note: ill means bad, as in ill luck

indicators.note: turning means the word is turned round, read backwards

parts.note: an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A crook having a rough time going straight, or rather turning left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses AGE to EGA. 'has' is a link word; 'Criminal' looks like a noun but is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Something criminal is against the law, that is, unlawful.

clue.text: Downland

parts.note: one word that splits into two senses: down (soft feathers, not heavy) and land (to settle on, to ...)

explanation.walkthrough: 'Downland' looks like a single word for rolling chalk hills; split it as 'Down' and 'land', each giving the same five-letter word.
explanation.definitionFit: Down feathers are weightless, not heavy, and a bird settling on a branch is said to alight on it.

clue.text: Loaded and under way

explanation.definitionFit: Someone rolling in it is very wealthy; cameras or a project start rolling when they get going.

clue.text: Discordant bars

definitions.meaning: a frame of parallel or crossed metal bars

explanation.definitionFit: A rasping noise jars on the ear; a framework of metal bars covers a drain or a window.

clue.text: Hunter's performance taking an age

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', so the hunter is the answer

parts.note: an act is a stage performance
an aeon is an age, an immensely long period

explanation.surface: A hunter's show that drags on forever.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth Actaeon was the hunter who saw Artemis bathing and was turned into a stag. 'taking' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek legend he was a huntsman, torn apart by his own hounds.

clue.text: Intimate the way to follow suit

definitions.meaning: close and personal, as of a frank talk
in card games you follow suit by playing the same suit, such as a heart to a heart

explanation.definitionFit: A frank, close conversation is a personal one; at cards, following suit means playing a red heart on a heart already led.
